source_text: Klagel. Jerem. 4, 12. Ἰσως μὲν καὶ διὰ τὸ τῶν τόπων ὀχυρὸν καὶ τοῦ τείχους καὶ τὴν τῶν οἰκητόρων ἰσχύν, μάλιστα δὲ διὰ τὸν ἀεὶ τῆς πόλεως ὑπερησπικότα θεόν. καίτοι πρὸ τοῦ Ναβουχοδονόσορ εἰσελθὼν ὁ Αἰγύπτιος πολλάκις ἔλαβε τοὺς θησαυροὺς ἐκ τοῦ οἴκου κυρίου, ἀλλ’ οὐ πορθήσας τὴν πόλιν· οὐ γὰρ ἄγαν ἔθλιβεν, εἰ καὶ ὑπῆρχεν ἐχθρός, πρὸς τὸ μηδὲ ἀπεμφαῖνον εἶναι καὶ δὶς καὶ τρὶς τὸ παράδοξον γενέσθαι. λέγοι δ’ ἂν βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς καὶ τοὺς δαίμονας τοὺς τῶν χοϊκῶν βασιλεύσαντας, περὶ ὡν εἴρηται· «παρέστησαν πάντες οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες αὐτῶν συνήχθησαν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ κατὰ τοῦ κυρίου καὶ κατὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ αὐτοῦ. περὶ ὡν οἴτινές εἰσιν ἐδήλωσε τὸ «εἰ γὰρ ἔγνωσαν, οὐκ ἂν τὸν κύριον τῆς δόξης ἐσταύρωσαν« καὶ τὸ «ἴνα γνωρισθῇ ταῖς ἀρχαῖς καὶ ταῖς ἐξουσίαις ἐν τοῖς ἐπουρανίοις διὰ τῆς ἐκκλησίας ἡ πολυποίκιλος σοφία τοῦ θεοῦ«· ᾤοντο γὰρ μὴ παραδίδοσθαι τὴν Ἱερουσαλὴμ εἰς τέλος, μέχρι τοῦ ἔθνους τούτου τὴν πρὸς τοὺς πατέρας ἐπαγγελίαν οἰόμενοι, μηδὲν εἰδότες περὶ Χριστοῦ.
pass_a_gloss: [Pass A] Perhaps both through the strength of the places and of the wall and the strength of the inhabitants, and especially through God who was always shielding the city. And yet before Nebuchadnezzar the Egyptian, having entered, many times took the treasures from the Lord’s house, but not having sacked the city; for he was not pressing very hard, even if he was an enemy—toward it not being inconsistent for the paradoxical thing to come about even twice and thrice. And he would also mean kings of the earth as the demons who ruled the earthy ones, about whom it has been said: “all the kings of the earth stood by and their rulers were gathered together against the Lord and against his Christ.” About who these are, “for if they had known, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory” made clear, and “so that the many-colored wisdom of God may be made known to the rulers and the authorities in the heavenlies through the church”; for they were thinking Jerusalem not to be handed over unto the end, thinking the promise toward the fathers as far as this nation, knowing nothing about Christ.
pass_b_english: Perhaps both through the strength of the places and of the wall and the strength of the inhabitants, and especially through God who was always shielding the city. And yet before Nebuchadnezzar the Egyptian, having entered, many times took the treasures from the Lord’s house, but not having sacked the city; for he was not pressing very hard, even if he was an enemy—toward it not being inconsistent for the paradoxical thing to come about even twice and thrice. And he would also mean kings of the earth as the demons who ruled the earthy ones, about whom it has been said: “all the kings of the earth stood by and their rulers were gathered together against the Lord and against his Christ.” (Lamentations 4:12) About who these are, “for if they had known, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory” (Psalm 2:2) made clear, and “so that the many-colored wisdom of God may be made known to the rulers and the authorities in the heavenlies through the church” (1 Corinthians 2:8); for they were thinking Jerusalem not to be handed over unto the end, thinking the promise toward the fathers as far as this nation, knowing nothing about Christ (Ephesians 3:10).

choices.why: Symmachus/Theodotion gloss Origen cites at Lam 4:7.
